texts.preamble: State vs Afzal on 18 November, 2025 State Vs. Afzal Fir No.: 86/2019 Ps: Anand Vihar In The Court Of Sh. Manish Jain Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Shahdara District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi Cnr No. Dlsh020065112023 A Case Identification 86/2019
texts.facts: The present case has been instituted on the basis of charge-sheet filed against the accused Afzal for the offences punishable under Sections 287/337/506 IPC, who is stated to be on bail. 2. In brief, the facts of the case as per the prosecution are that on 06.03.2019, victim Dilshad was admitted to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital with burn injuries from a gas stove/fire incident at Bharat Chicken, Karkardooma. He stated that he was heating the chulha for preparing chicken rolls when the gas leaked and caught fire and the manager Mukhtar had been informed earlier about the leakage but no safety measures were taken. No owner/manager accompanied him to the hospital. MLC and statements confirmed injuries due to negligent handling of gas equipment. Police seized the gas cylinder and chulha. Owner Afjal later produced his trade and food safety licences. After investigation, chargesheet under Sections 286/337/506 IPC was filed for negligence and unsafe conditions at the shop. Anand Vihar 09.06.2023 took the cognizance of the offences against accused. Upon appearance of accused, copy of chargesheet was supplied to the accused and he was admitted to bail. 4. Thereafter, charge was framed vide order dated 27.02.2024 against accused for the offences punishable u/s 287/337/506 IPC to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the matter was put up for prosecution evidence. 5. Prosecution has examined PW-1 Dilshad, who is the complainant in this case, who deposed that on 06.03.2019, he was working as a chef at the shop of the accused Afzal which was his first day of work. He was preparing chicken rolls at the shop situated near Karkardooma Metro Station. At about 04:00 PM, while he attempted to light the gas stove using a matchstick, the stove caught fire and he sustained burn injuries on his face. He stated that thereafter he called his uncle, Md. Nasim, who reached the spot around 04:30 PM, after which he became unconscious. PW-1 deposed that he can identify the accused however, the identity of accused remained undisputed by the defence. He further stated that he had not given any statement to the police officials. Since the witness was not disclosing the complete facts, Ld. APP was permitted to put leading questions. On being confronted with his statement Ex. PW1/A, the witness denied having made such a statement to the police. When confronted with portions A to A-1 and B to B-1 of Ex. PW1/A, the witness denied the same and further denied having informed the accused or Manager Mukhtar that the gas pipe was leaking or required repair. He denied the recording of any supplementary statement Mark X by the police. He also denied that the site plan Ex. PW1/B or the seizure memo Ex. PW1/C (chulha, cylinder and regulator) were prepared or effected at his instance. He further denied the suggestion that the accused Afzal had threatened him with dire consequences by saying that he would terminate him from service or get him killed, as mentioned in Mark X. He again denied the confronted portions A to A-1 and B to B-1 of Mark X. During cross- examination , PW-1 denied having informed Manager Mukhtar or Afzal about any gas leakage earlier. PW-1 further failed to identify the case property (gas stove, cylinder, regulator) when shown in court. PW-1 was cross examined by Ld. counsel for accused. 6. PW-2 Naseem, uncle of the injured Dilshad, stated that he does not know anything about the present case and that the police officials had not recorded his statement. He further stated that he is unable to identify the accused, even if he is present in court. In his cross-examination by the Ld. APP, PW-2 stated that he is illiterate. PW-2 denied all confronted portions and further denied that he was suppressing facts, had compromised with the accused, or was deposing falsely. PW-2 was cross examined by Ld. counsel for accused. This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for accused.
texts.arguments: 11.It is argued by Ld. Counsel for accused that since the complainant did not support the case of prosecution for the allegations so leveled against the accused, accused may be acquitted for the offences he is charged for.
